subject: gk
question: Who among the following has written the book ‘Three Thousand Stitches: Ordinary People, Extraordinary Lives’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sudha Murty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sudha Murthy** is an** Indian philanthropist** and** writer in Kannada and English.**
 
• Her book **Three Thousand Stitches is a collection of 11 short stories** that draw from **her real life experiences, as an individual and as the chairperson of Infosys Foundation, which works for the underprivileged.**
 
• Sudha Murthy is **an engineer and writes in Kannada, Marathi and English and is also a social worker. **
 
• She is the** chairperson of Infosys Foundation and is married to N Narayana Murthy, co-founder of Infosys.**
 
• **Books-** Three thousand stitches, Mahashweta, Astitva, The mother I never knew, etc.
 
• **Awards- **Padma Shri (2006), Basava Shri (2013), etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Arundhati Roy__

 __
 
• She is an Indian author, writer, and essayist.
 
• She is also a political activist involved in human rights and environmental causes.
 
• Roy has campaigned along with activist Medha Patkar against the Narmada dam project.
 
• She believed that the dam will displace half a million people with little or no compensation, and will not provide the projected irrigation, drinking water, and other benefits.
 
• She has also been awarded the Sydney Peace Prize in 2004.
 
• Some of her other books are:__
 __
 
• The Algebra of Infinite Justice, 2002
 
• The ministry of Utmost Happiness, 2017
 
 
 
 
 
• Anita Nair__
 
 
• **She is an Indian novelist.**
 
• She is best known for her **English novels, poetry, essays, short stories, crime fiction, historical fiction, romance, and children's literature.**
 
• Her famous works are A Better Man, Mistress and Lessons in Forgetting.
